author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it by full name, on one unpaged page reachable by its URL alone.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when GET /specialties.html is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name on a single page with no pagination
given a specialty held by veterinarians, when the specialty directory is opened, then each holder is listed under it by first name then last name, for example "Helen Leary"
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears under no specialty
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the specialty directory is opened, then the specialty is listed and shown as having no veterinarians
given a veterinarian holding several specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then the veterinarian appears under each one
given the specialty directory, when it is opened twice, then specialties and the veterinarians under each appear in the same stable order
given any other page of the system, when it is rendered, then it carries no navigation entry or link to the specialty directory
given the supported languages, when the wording is checked, then every new piece of page wording is present in every one of them and none is hard-coded into the page
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties (NG-2, unchanged): the page is read-only
a navigation entry or a link from any other page to the specialty directory; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request
filtering or searching specialties or veterinarians on the page (NG-9)
a machine-readable form of the specialty directory
notes: Grounded in intake-decision line 1. Primary surface: code change. Boundary check: NG-2 unchanged (owner decision quoted in intake); no Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. REQ-SYS-001 still holds: the new page carries the shared navigation, and no entry for itself is added. Decided by me as reversible, narrowest reading: a specialty with no holders is still listed (the request says 'every specialty the clinic knows') and is shown as having none, mirroring REQ-VET-001; the order is stable but unspecified, so the design picks it. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions: a visible entry point (follow-up) and the exact presentation order. The multi-specialty case and the i18n bullet carry no dedicated test name: the holder test's data can cover the multi-specialty case, and the existing I18nPropertiesSyncTest covers the bundle-completeness half.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure, § Contracts) using only in-force patterns (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog). The small adjustment: the listing needs every specialty the clinic knows, including unheld ones, which no current read exposes, so a read-only SpecialtyRepository is added on the PetTypeRepository lookup-value precedent. Grouping and ordering are a domain derivation, not a controller rule (Web controller row), so they live in an immutable value object SpecialtyDirectory in the vet package. VetController gains GET /specialties.html, which reads both repositories, builds SpecialtyDirectory, and selects view vets/specialtyList; the template uses the shared layout with no menu entry. Order decision (PRD Open Question, design-picked, reversible): specialties by name; holders by last name, then first name, then identity. Basis: grep of the vet package and PetTypeRepository; IDE oracle not connected.
integration_points: SpecialtyRepository extends Spring Data Repository<Specialty, Integer>, not JpaRepository, and exposes one @Transactional(readOnly = true) read returning all specialties in name order. It has no save or delete, keeping NG-2 read-only. Uncached; CacheConfiguration is unchanged.

SpecialtyDirectory: a static factory over (specialties, veterinarians) returns an immutable directory of entries (specialty name, holder full names as 'first last'), using List.copyOf. It references no mutable entity after construction (architecture-principles § Domain Core, Value object row).
Holders come from VetRepository.findAll() (cached 'vets', eager specialties). No new query and no inverse mapping are added.
Binding: GET /specialties.html binds no request parameter and no persisted type. The handler takes only the Model; no @InitBinder is needed.
Double, repository boundary in SpecialtyDirectoryTests: none. The tests build real Vet and Specialty objects (testing-principles § Mocking Policy).

Double, repository boundary in VetControllerTests: a hand-written in-memory SpecialtyRepository registered through a nested @TestConfiguration. The class's existing @MockitoBean VetRepository stub is the tolerated legacy seam and supplies the vets; add no new Mockito stub for SpecialtyRepository.

Double, framework transport: MockMvc via @WebMvcTest, which renders Thymeleaf. The no-navigation-entry test asserts that rendered HTML of pages carrying the shared layout (e.g. /vets.html) contains no reference to /specialties.html.

Wording: the page heading and any new label become new message keys in every bundle under src/main/resources/messages/ (REQ-LANG-002, enforced by I18nPropertiesSyncTest). The empty-holder case reuses the existing 'none' key, as vetList.html does.

patterns.description: layout use, th:text output, #{none} for an empty specialty cell

risks.risk: Specialty inherits no equals/hashCode from BaseEntity. Instances from SpecialtyRepository and those inside cached Vet objects are different objects, so matching by object equality would leave every specialty with no holders.
risks.mitigation: Match holders by specialty id (system-design § Contracts invariants line). SpecialtyDirectoryTests builds specialties as separate instances sharing an id.

risks.risk: Adding an inverse @ManyToMany on Specialty would change the eager graph and cycle the serialized /vets output.
risks.mitigation: Specialty stays unchanged. Holders are derived from Vet.getSpecialties() (system-design § Contracts invariants line).

risks.risk: The specialty directory path scales with the specialty and vet counts (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty directory row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: in-memory grouping and sorting over the two full collections, with no paging.

risks.risk: Stored names are rendered into HTML (system-design § Threat Model, cross-site scripting row).
risks.mitigation: Render with th:text only, never th:utext (security-principles § Language Realization).

risks.risk: Stable order across requests (PRD edge case). Set iteration order inside Vet is not stable.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory sorts both levels explicitly, with identity as the final tie-break. A test asserts the order on input deliberately supplied unsorted.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. docs/system-design.md had no § Scale and Load section. It is added with the specialty directory row only, per demand-driven foundation; the existing vet-list path has no row yet. Contracts rows now carry REQ-VET-003 for Vet, Specialty, VetRepository, VetController, and the new SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyDirectory. For the product expert, not blocking: 'specialty directory' is used in the PRD but has no ubiquitous-language entry, and SpecialtyDirectory is named from the PRD's wording. The chosen order answers the PRD Open Question provisionally; the owner may revise it. PRD file_targets list only messages.properties, but REQ-LANG-002 requires every locale bundle.

author: code-quality-reviewer
recommendations: src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/SpecialtyRepository.java findSpecialties: the query's `ORDER BY specialty.name` and its Javadoc 'in name order' duplicate the ordering SpecialtyDirectory.of re-applies with BY_SPECIALTY_NAME, which also breaks ties by id. The repository ordering is redundant for this consumer. A later reader may not know which one is authoritative. Consider dropping the ORDER BY, or stating on the repository that the directory is authoritative. This is polish and not required to merge.
approved_aspects: Design placement: grouping and ordering of holders live in the immutable SpecialtyDirectory value object, matching its row in docs/system-design.md Contracts (`SpecialtyDirectory | Immutable value object listing every specialty with its holders' full names`); VetController only reads and renders (SpecialtyDirectory.of(...) call in showSpecialtyDirectory), so no rule lands in the controller.

Scope: VetController adds only the `/specialties.html` mapping; the diff shows no navigation or link change to the layout or other templates, consistent with the REQ-VET-003 bullet that the page is reached by address alone.

Vocabulary: Specialty, Veterinarian and holder match docs/ubiquitous-language.md (Veterinarian 'holds' Specialties); none of the Avoid terms (Skill, Qualification, Discipline) appear in the new names.

Workload Fit: the system-design Scale and Load row for the specialty directory records in-memory grouping over the two full collections, and SpecialtyDirectory.of is a single groupingBy pass plus two sorts, which fits it. There is no repository call in a loop and no N+1.

Comments: the three Javadoc blocks in SpecialtyDirectory and the two in SpecialtyRepository (conventions-map hits) explain why. The specialty-id matching note says Specialty has no value equality and the vet's instances differ from the read's. No requirement ids or handoff vocabulary appear in code comments.
Records: SpecialtyDirectory and Entry use compact constructors with List.copyOf for defensive copies, and the creator takes every mandatory parameter.
Format: `./gradlew checkFormat` passes. The `checkJavaFormat` task named in the agent definition does not exist in this project, so the project's own `checkFormat` task was run instead.
Template: specialtyList.html reuses the `vets` and `none` keys already in messages.properties (lines `vets=Veterinarians`, `none=none`), and the holder join mirrors the existing vetList.html idiom.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Input surface: the new route takes no request input. VetController.java:68 `public String showSpecialtyDirectory(Model model) {` has no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, @ModelAttribute or @RequestBody, so it adds no binding target and no mass-assignment surface. It is a GET-only read and mutates nothing.

Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository.java:35 `@Query("SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name")` is a static JPQL string with no concatenated or request-derived value. The repository extends the bare `Repository` (line 28) and declares no save or delete, so it grants only read access.

XSS and output escaping: specialtyList.html renders stored values only through escaped `th:text`. Line 18 is `th:text="${entry.specialtyName}"` and line 21 is `th:text="${holder.last ? holderName : holderName + ', '}"`. `grep -rn -F -e 'th:utext' -e '__${' src/main/resources/templates/` returns no hit in vets/specialtyList.html, so the template uses no unescaped output and no preprocessing. Its hits are pre-existing ones in other templates.

Exposed surface: the change adds one read-only HTML endpoint, /specialties.html. It exposes specialty names and vet full names, which /vets.html and /vets already publish. Management exposure is unchanged.

Resource bounds: the unpaged full read matches the existing /vets route, VetController.java:80 `vets.getVetList().addAll(this.vetRepository.findAll());`. It is recorded as bounded in the new system-design.md Scale and Load row. findAll stays @Cacheable (VetRepository.java:45 `@Cacheable("vets")`), so the change adds no new unbounded-allocation surface. SpecialtyDirectory copies its lists into immutable ones (List.copyOf) and holds no shared mutable state.

Secrets and errors: the diff adds no credential, token or connection string. Its message-bundle additions are only the `specialtyDirectory` and `specialty` labels in all ten bundles (checked with git diff of src/main/resources/messages). It adds no new exception message and no logging.

Supply chain: build.gradle is unchanged (git diff --stat empty), so no dependency was added. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (no `dependencyCheck` hit in build.gradle), so no NVD match ran in this review. The resolved runtime versions are Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9 and jackson-databind 3.1.5 (from ./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath).

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: The change stays in the vet package: one new GET route on VetController, a new read-only repository and value object, one template, two message keys in each of the ten bundles, and PRD and system-design additions. No sensitive paths, no layout or navigation edits, no build changes, and the existing vet routes keep their behavior apart from the extra constructor argument.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading SpecialtyDirectory.of, holders are grouped by specialty id (needed because Specialty has no value equality), specialties are sorted by name then id, and holders by last name, first name, then id. Names render first then last as the PRD asks. A specialty no vet holds falls back to an empty list and renders the existing none key. Output goes through escaped th:text. The DB ORDER BY is redundant because the Java sort is authoritative, but it changes nothing. No inverted condition or hidden behavior change found.

test_adequacy.note: SpecialtyDirectoryTests compares whole directory objects with real Vet and Specialty instances, and builds a fresh Specialty per call so the tests would fail if matching fell back to instance identity. They cover a holder of several specialties, a vet with none, a specialty with no holders, and unsorted input on both levels. The MockMvc tests check the route, view, rendered names, the none marker, and that the shared-layout page has no link. The one gap is the id tie-break, which no test exercises; it is not a PRD rule.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers in the dispatched roster approved in round 1, but doc-reviewer approved with two open clarify findings: ubiquitous-language.md has no entry for 'specialty directory' or 'holder', and system-design.md:36 still describes vet/ as 'entities, repository, controller'. I confirmed the line 36 text is still there. Code-quality (redundant ORDER BY) and test (untested id tie-break) attached polish-level recommendations. The cited lines I checked resolve; security's VetController.java:68 points at the @GetMapping line, one above the method signature it quotes.

scope_deviation.note: No design revisions, consultations, or build retries. The diff covers exactly the PRD surface: one unpaged read-only page reachable only by its address, with no navigation entry, wording in every bundle, and a stable order. No fix-round delta and no business rule beyond the ones recorded in the PRD and the design rows.

rationale: The code is small, contained, and well tested, and reading it turned up no behavioral surprise. The only flag is reviewer hedging: doc-reviewer approved but left two documentation gaps open (vocabulary entries, a stale vet package line). Skim the code, and decide whether to fix those two doc items before merging.
